name: Hoshea
overview: Hoshea was a male figure known primarily as the son of Elah who assassinated King Pekah and subsequently became King of Israel. His rise to power marks a significant transition in the leadership of Israel, as recorded in the Old Testament. There is no information on his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Hoshea' means 'salvation' in Hebrew, reflecting a meaningful designation though it was not given by God. He also held the title 'King of Israel,' which straightforwardly identifies his royal role in the nation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hoshea was the son of Elah. Additionally, he is noted as the killer of King Pekah, indicating a direct and violent interaction with his predecessor. Beyond these, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Hoshea's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his role in the political upheaval of Israel, where he took the throne by killing the reigning king, Pekah. This act and his subsequent reign highlight a turbulent period in Israel's history. His story underscores themes of leadership change and divine sovereignty over the kings of Israel.
